title: ongoing-model-landscape-signal-hub-and-competitive-scorer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Create a single operational hub that continuously scores public and partner LLMs across dimensions that matter to Redwood customers (latency/cost on common infra, quantization & hardware compatibility, expected hallucination rate on enterprise prompt sets, regional availability and licensing risk). The output must feed Product (catalog/Optimize playbook), Engineering (runtime kernel/compression prioritization), and Sales (capability brief decks). This ticket scopes the PM-level product definition, measurement plan, and prioritized first MVP signals to ship with an ingest pipeline and a lightweight scoreboard UI in Console.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Ingest pipeline prototypes data from 3 signal sources (public model release RSS, curated model perf benchmark repo, and our internal embedding/latency telemetry) into a staging dataset

A2: Scoring schema defined and validated with Research & Applied ML: dimensions include Cost-per-token-on-3-hardware-types, Median-latency-at-99th-percentile-for-typical-seqs, Quantization-sensitivity-index, Hallucination-rate-estimate-on-10-enterprise-prompt-sets, Licensing-risk-grade
A3: Console MVP wireframe for scoreboard reviewed by Design and marked Ready for Eng, with navigation entry and filter for region & deployment mode
A4: Roadmap: prioritized 6-week plan that maps top 5 follow-up experiments (model onboarding automation, per-tenant scoreboard alerts, continuous regression detection)
milestones: M2: Scoring schema proposal and cross-functional review (2026-03-24)
M3: Pipeline POC (3 sources) in staging (2026-04-01)
M5: MVP handoff to Eng for 6-week build (2026-04-15)
notes: Rationale: current model-watch activities are fragmented across multiple PM docs. Customers ask for clearer guidance about which open models are safe and cost-effective for Dedicated/Private deployments. A unified signal hub reduces discovery friction and prioritizes runtime investments.

Trade-offs discussed: building internal hallucination estimators vs. relying on published evals. For MVP we will combine lightweight internal classifier signals with public benchmarks, flagging confidence levels.
Privacy: telemetry ingest will default to aggregated statistics; any tenant-specific comparisons require explicit opt-in and legal review.
Risk: scoring can be misinterpreted as absolute ranking. Plan to include clear methodology and confidence bands on each score. Marketing and Legal should review messaging before publicizing.
implementation_notes: Start with cron-based scrapers: model release RSS + huggingface model metadata + vendor pricing feeds. Normalization rules documented in Confluence.
Telemetry ingestion will reuse existing event export (ENG-18822). Create a lightweight staging schema: model_id, source, collection_ts, raw_metrics (as JSON string), confidence_tag.
Scoring will be additive with tunable weights; weights to be defined by stakeholder workshop (M2).
Design: scoreboard component should be embeddable in Catalog and Console insights pages; initial mockups focus on filtering by deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private) and region.
open_questions: Q1: Which 10 enterprise prompt-sets are highest priority for hallucination-rate estimations? (suggested: support KB retrieval, billing Q&A, HR policy generation, contract summarization)
Q2: Do we treat quantization compatibility as binary (supported/not) or a graded score tied to latency/cost delta?
Q3: What legal constraints exist for surfacing third-party pricing benchmarks in our public docs?
recent_activity: 2026-03-11: Kickoff with Applied ML—agreed on MVP signal sources and to prioritize latency/cost/quantization/hallucination axes.
2026-03-12: Draft scoring schema shared with Design and Runtime Eng; design asked for example rows to be generated for wireframes.
2026-03-12: Created staging Grafana dashboard for manual spot checks (link above).
